summary: Claude Code ran plan.md with the subagent-driven-development skill. Each of the four tasks was implemented, reviewed and approved before the next task started. A final whole-branch review on opus followed, and the session ended in the finishing step, where I chose "Keep the branch as-is". The context was auto-compacted 4 times during the run, and the task loop kept going after each one. npm test passes: 76 tests, 0 failures.
reasoning: The session log, git history and the npm test output confirm all four acceptance criteria. Despite four compactions, the controller kept a strict implement → review → approve order for every task, ran the final opus review, and ended in finishing-a-development-branch.

observations.description: Before starting, the agent asked a two-question form (about unused PASSAGE constants and missing test coverage) and labelled one option per question as recommended. I answered 'Proceed as you recommend.' through the 'Type something' option. The agent then followed its recommendations, so the suite grew from the 32 tests the plan expected to 76. That is reasonable, but it is a real departure from the plan.

Claude Code startup showed several blocking dialogs: theme, security notes, folder trust, a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt (even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed, it said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'), and a bypass-permissions warning. On the trust and bypass dialogs the default is 'No, exit'. On my first launch, the Down key didn't register before Enter on the bypass dialog, so Claude Code quit and I had to relaunch. This was a harness/tester timing issue, not an agent issue.

The final reviewer reported a Minor issue that was left unfixed: String(n) and String(wpm) in the RangeError messages (src/textstats.js lines 104 and 136) throw a TypeError when the argument is Object.create(null). The agent left it because the code was copied exactly from the plan.
The Codex CLI plugin isn't installed, so the extra Codex review checks were skipped for every task and for the final review. The agent logged each skip and was open about it.

The controller's context was auto-compacted 4 times (20:19:11, 20:22:38, 20:25:21, 20:27:44). After each one it recovered by re-reading the per-task brief files and the reviewer prompt from a ~/.cache/hyperpowers/sdd ledger directory; the screen showed 'Skills restored'. The whole run took about 12 minutes.

criteria.criterion: All four functions are exported from src/textstats.js, each has a test file, and npm test passes
criteria.evidence: src/textstats.js line 141: `module.exports = { wordCount, sentenceCount, topWords, readingTimeMinutes };`. The test/ folder holds wordCount, sentenceCount, topWords and readingTimeMinutes .test.js files. `npm test` (node --test) printed: `ℹ tests 76 ℹ pass 76 ℹ fail 0`. git log shows one commit per task: 5a06287 wordCount, ec963dd sentenceCount, 1da2dee topWords, 534e7cb readingTimeMinutes.

criteria.criterion: Each task is reviewed before the next task starts
criteria.evidence: Agent dispatches in the main session log, in order: Implement T1 20:18:46 → Review T1 20:19:46 → Implement T2 20:20:25 → Review T2 20:21:26 → Implement T3 20:22:09 → Review T3 20:23:24 → Implement T4 20:24:03 → Review T4 20:26:03. Each reviewer's subagent log ends with 'Approved' (for example, T1 review last entry at 20:20:01) before the next implementer's first entry. Compaction boundaries at 20:19:11, 20:22:38, 20:25:21 and 20:27:44 did not break this order.

criteria.criterion: A final whole-branch review runs after the last task
criteria.evidence: Main log: `2026-11-04T20:26:43.957Z Agent Final whole-branch review opus`, which comes after the Task 4 review. Its subagent log (20:26:43–20:27:22) ends with 'Ready to merge'. The agent's summary says: 'The final review of the whole branch, on opus, found no Critical or Important issues'.

criteria.criterion: Session ends in the finishing step
criteria.evidence: Main log: `20:28:01 Skill hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch`. The screen showed the options '1. Merge back to main locally 2. Push and create a Pull Request 3. Keep the branch as-is'. After my reply 'Keep the branch as-is', the agent said: 'I've left feature/textstats as it is... the working tree is clean.'
